Hi Eli — thanks for the screenshots and the header dump, that helps. I’m looping in Ben (eng) and Laura (sales) to investigate. Quick asks while we triage: can you confirm if the invite was sent to eli@shipwright.com or to an alias (eli.navarro@shipwright.com / procurement@shipwright.com)? Also, can you try opening the link in an Incognito window and share the exact URL it lands on?

Ben — initial observation: the URL in the screenshot has an extra query param that looks like a routing token from our invite service. Their redirect shows a buyer-tenant slug (buyer-zencrest) that doesn't match Shipwright. My guess is the link is being rewritten by their mail gateway or there's tenant collision on Ariba side.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben: check the invite token mapping and server logs for the token in the header dump (I attached).
- If we can’t resolve quickly, issue a temporary manual invite link (short-lived) and paste it into the thread for Eli to use.
- Laura: inform the AM so procurement holds off on sending the PO until invite is accepted.

Eli — we’ll aim to get a manual link out within a couple hours.

—Tessa

Thanks for the context. I pulled the logs for the invite token referenced in the header dump. Observations:

- Our invite service generated token=RWI-4f7a and the initial link is https://supplier.ariba.com/invite?token=RWI-4f7a&src=redwood.
- In the request chain the Host header is unchanged but the gateway adds an X-Forwarded-For and their MX appears to rewrite the envelope recipient to procurement@shipwright.com (see header dump).
- The redirect to buyer-zencrest happens when Ariba resolves the token against the account namespace — token collision is unlikely, but the gateway rewrite means the request ends up scoped to procurement@shipwright.com which is provisioned under a different buyer tenant in their system.

Proposed remediation options (ordered by speed):
1) Manual one-time invite: create a direct invite URL that maps token->explicit tenant id and expires in 12 hours. I can generate and post it in this thread; Eli can accept immediately. (fastest)
2) Reissue invite using a different claimant email (eli+rw@shipwright.com) to bypass gateway rewriting/aliases.
3) Ask Shipwright IT to whitelist our sending domain and stop envelope rewriting — higher friction, slower.

I'll generate a manual link now and include a short troubleshooting checklist for the Shipwright IT team if this recurs. Also attaching the header dump I parsed.

Attachments: manual-invite-link.txt (contains one-time URL), parsed-header-dump.txt

Subject: Re: Can't accept Ariba supplier invite — link redirects to another org

Tessa / Ben / Laura — manual link worked, thank you. We accepted the invite and completed the onboarding steps in Ariba. I attached a screenshot of the confirmation page.

For Shipwright IT: the gateway had been normalizing recipient addresses to procurement@shipwright.com for all inbound mail to the procurement group; that normalization was causing the Ariba token to be scoped incorrectly. We disabled that normalization for redwood.com and the issue went away.

Outcome / notes:
- Manual link: accepted at 2027-06-14 16:12 PDT (attached).
- We uploaded the W-9 and are ready for PO issuance.
- If you want to avoid rework: Ben's suggestion to issue invites using the explicit tenant-id param is a good fallback.

Thanks for the quick help — appreciate the follow-up.

Best,
Eli Navarro
Procurement Lead
Shipwright Logistics
